candidates.reason: The exact-timestamped announcement is inside the priority window and the 40-page company preprint discloses a consequential, non-duplicate evaluation result: ten reruns missed the defining array because the relevant upstream DNA never reached model context. Earlier independent phage studies and an independent methodological reading support a bounded deployment analysis without claiming biological replication.

The release is inside the 48-hour discovery window but outside the 24-hour priority window. It is consequential, but the fresher ART evidence offers a clearer non-duplicate operational lesson; future coverage would require current independent task-level evaluation and migration analysis.
Discovery results were marketing and funding coverage without enough primary technical evidence or independent measurement to support a 1,200-word article.

candidates.reason: Recent Index Us articles and public run records already cover these developments. No correction or materially new primary evidence was found in this run.

decision.reason: Anthropic's ART campaign is fresh, consequential and not already covered. The article turns the disclosed reproducibility failure into a bounded operator decision: research-agent evaluations should measure the route from stored evidence to model context, repeat the end-to-end campaign and preserve independent validation, while keeping the company-authored, unreviewed biological result and its unknown function explicit.

claims.text: Anthropic's ART announcement was posted at 18:18:33.678 UTC on 23 September 2026, inside the run's priority window.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 retained post metadata and public X snowflake timestamp.

claims.text: The broad campaign used Mythos 5, 949 agent sessions, 119 tasks, 76.9 agent-hours, 215.6 million tokens and 21.5 hours of wall time.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 Results pages 2–3 and Methods pages 28–30.

claims.text: The campaign surveyed about 1.9 billion protein clusters, retained 198,290 reverse-transcriptase clusters and produced 19 reports.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 abstract, Results pages 2–4 and Methods pages 28–30.

claims.text: A worker rejected the initial gene association but queued the reverse transcriptase for follow-up; its supervisor directed the next worker to inspect the upstream region, where the defining array was noticed after the DNA entered model context.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 Results pages 3–5, Supplementary Figure 2 and transcript-analysis method page 30; supported as the authors' retained-session reconstruction.

claims.text: Human-directed analysis identified 95 ART-family clusters and detectable upstream arrays in 28.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 Results pages 5–7 and Methods pages 31–32.

claims.text: Earlier independent papers described the MarsHill reverse transcriptase and the SA1 transcriptomic dataset, but did not independently verify Anthropic's ART interpretation.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 MarsHill genomic analysis; s6 SA1 abstract and methods; s3 Discussion page 14 and RNA-seq method page 34.

claims.text: ART's biological function remains unknown; the work did not establish reverse-transcriptase activity, RNA substrates, reverse-transcriptase–partner interaction or a gene-editing capability.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 ART section; s3 Discussion page 13; s4 independent announcement summary.

claims.text: Ten reruns missed the defining array because none read the relevant upstream DNA, despite most completed reruns sampling ART loci.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 Results pages 8–10; the identifier-bounded search limitation remains stated in the review.

claims.text: The fixed-input tests covered seven Claude models, five information levels and 100 attempts per model and level, judged by Mythos 5 against ten curated features.

The four most capable models recognised the array in at least 90 per cent of direct-context attempts; file-and-tool conditions could fall to 32 per cent; 39 per cent of relevant file attempts never read 200 contiguous nucleotides; reading at least 200 nucleotides raised recognition by 16–32 percentage points per model.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 Results pages 9–10 and Figure 4; scoped to Anthropic's internal benchmark.

claims.text: Tool availability does not guarantee evidence access, so evidence-access instrumentation should be part of research-agent evaluation.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us operational synthesis from c08–c10, presented as an operator recommendation rather than a universal experimental result.

claims.text: Independent biological replication, peer review and enough campaign artefacts to test the original discovery path would materially strengthen the finding.
claims.sourceLocator: Editorial judgement derived from the primary report's limits and the independent-source boundary.

claims.text: Index Us did not run the campaign, access Mythos 5, analyse the sequence data, reproduce the benchmark or perform laboratory work.
claims.sourceLocator: Run process fact, with s3 identifying the external campaign, model, analyses, benchmark and experiments reviewed.

claims.text: Eleven campaigns are too few to estimate a stable discovery rate; the evidence establishes one observed success and the mechanism of the misses, not a transferable probability.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 rerun evidence and s7 independent methodological reading; no numerical success-rate estimate is published.
